title: Structural Mechanics
description: Steel stretches in proportion to the stress on it (Hooke, σ = Eε) until it yields; but a slender column fails long before that, by bowing sideways. Euler found the load at which it buckles: P = π²EI/(KL)². Stiffness against buckling comes from the shape of the section, its second moment I, which is why beams are I-shaped. Unlocks the Load Test Rig and Rated I-Beams.

puzzle.goal: A slender column of length L, pinned at both ends, of a material of modulus E and a section of second moment I. Write the load P at which it buckles.
puzzle.name: Euler's buckling load
puzzle.ask: Find P in newtons for a steel column: E = @{E} Pa, I = @{I} m⁴, L = @{L} m.
puzzle.method: EI·y″ + P·y = 0 with y = 0 at both ends: the first mode, y = sin(πx/L), needs P = π²EI/L².
